To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ERP has been researched from six major perspectives: ERP systems, ERP implementation, ERP benefits, ERP risks, ERP adoption, and ERP success.

(1) the literature has grown at a very fast rate in terms of the number of papers published; (2) the literature is mainly focused on the implementation of ERP; (3) the literature is dominated by case studies, which is a reflection of the lack of theoretical development in the area; (4) most of the research is descriptive in nature; and (5) there is a lack of empirical research on the impact of ERP on organizational performance
the literature is dominated by the themes of implementation and benefits of ERP systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact of ERP on organizational effectiveness, the implementation of ERP systems, the adoption of ERP, the evaluation and measurement of ERP, the impact of ERP implementation on organizational performance and the impact of ERP systems on organizational culture.
the development of a framework to support the implementation of ERP systems.
the following questions: What are the main research themes? What are the main issues addressed? How are they addressed? What are the major findings? What research gaps exist?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERP research has been conducted in many countries, in many different industries, using many different methods.
the ERP literature is in its infancy.
ERP is a complex phenomenon that is difficult to understand, implement and manage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERP has evolved from a system to manage the business process to a tool for strategic decision support.

the literature has focused more on the adoption of the ERP systems and the impact of the ERP systems on business performance, while less work has been done on the impact of the systems on organizational performance.
ERP has been studied from the perspective of implementation, adoption, and impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERP literature is still in a nascent stage.
there has been a significant growth in the literature on ERP.
ERP is a very active research area and that the research questions addressed have evolved over the period under review.
